ruling: RULING 103 — a class sweep covers duplicated implementations, not only named instances
whatThisIs: The BASELINE, not an approval. tests/duplicate-implementations.test.ts fails on a duplicate group that is NOT recorded here, so the class cannot grow while the backlog is worked. Every entry carries a disposition and a reason; an entry with no reason fails, because an entry that says nothing has quietly become permission.
consolidatedOn2026-08-23: sourceUserAgent — four byte-identical copies of 'who is calling' across lib/sources/http.ts, congress, plural and legistar. CLAUDE.md makes an identified User-Agent with a contact address law; four copies is four places for that claim to drift. Now one, imported. Legistar's PACING stayed local on purpose — its spacing and retry budget were measured against Legistar.

personKey — scripts/photo-person-audit.mts carried a byte-identical copy under the name normalizePersonName. The audit that CHECKS one-person-one-photo was using a different definition of a person from the resolver it audits.

groups.reason: The production copy validates CRCs in official ZIP members; the test-only copy independently constructs raw ZIP fixtures. Importing the production checksum into that fixture builder would make the parser manufacture its expected CRC with the implementation under test and erase the corruption oracle. No second production path exists.

The production copy verifies the CRC declared by an official NJ OLS ZIP archive, while the test-only copy independently constructs stored-ZIP fixtures and then corrupts their payload bytes. Importing the production checksum into the fixture builder would make the decoder manufacture its own expected CRC and remove an independent corruption oracle; the test helper is not executable runtime authority.

The production helper derives the official roll-call URL it requires, while the test-only helper independently constructs source-receipt inputs. Sharing it would let an incorrect production URL validate against itself; the duplicate is an isolated oracle and has no runtime authority.

A one-line NextRequest test-fixture builder — request(origin, cookie) → new NextRequest(...) — repeated across the two fleet Admin tests (page, route). Trivial and test-local; consolidation into a shared tests/helpers builder is owed. It is fixture code, never shipped.

A .mjs helper run under plain node cannot import TypeScript, and scripts/tracker.mjs, scripts/handoff.mjs and the pre-commit hook all run without tsx. Consolidating would either break the hook or move the date rule into a module the hook cannot read. Both bodies compute the Phoenix day identically and tests/doc-dates.test.ts pins the rule itself.
Two copies of the same derived-index loader. One lazy loader for the zip-division index.
Same as inRing above — the test reimplements its subject.
Two text normalisers in the same subsystem. The ask box matches against one and digests against the other; a divergence would route a question one way and record it another.

582 characters of CSV parsing, twice, and scripts/doc-dates.mjs exports a third. The tracker stores are CSV; a parser that disagrees with itself about a quoted cell is a tracker that disagrees with itself about a row.
XML entity unescaping, twice, under two names.
Three tests each load the committed features their own way. A shared fixture loader is the fix.
Two guards walk the tree with their own copy of the walker. RULING 27 and RULING 59 both depend on that walk reaching every file; two walkers is two populations.

These are typed boundary lookups over three distinct authoritative registries: standing routine IDs, SOURCE_WIRING-derived meeting-partition IDs, and manual-production IDs have different types and fail-closed error codes. Each wrapper delegates the lookup to its own registry; a generic would erase useful type and diagnostic distinctions without consolidating policy.

This is the small header-column selection idiom in two different execution models: the production acquisition parses a verified in-memory archive, while the offline engineering extractor streams an unpacked workbook. They share no authority, state, or parsing lifecycle, and parameterizing the loop would add a cross-layer dependency rather than remove policy drift.

This collision exists only after domain identifiers are erased: adaptedSplit counts registry adaptation states, while the two roster helpers enforce source-specific legislative calendars, base legislature numbers, and term bounds. AZ changes on its official first-Monday rule and NJ on its statutory second-Tuesday rule, so parameterizing those authorities together—or coupling either to a jurisdiction census—would hide source law rather than consolidate shared policy; their genuinely shared ordinal formatter is imported from lib/text/format-date.ts.

Each adapter delegates to a different domain validator and only supplies its projection-specific diagnostic. The repeated issues-and-throw shell contains no validation rule; sharing it would merely parameterize a callback and noun while obscuring which authority refused its payload.

These are intentional typed source adapters around the single shared readPromotedOrBootstrap authority. Each binds a different source class, scope, validator, first-seed package, and isolated cache; combining the adapters would risk cross-source state while duplicating none of the store, proof, bootstrap, or fail-closed policy.

These are source-named preload bindings used by routes and tests. They delegate the canonical read and shared CivicDataStoreUnavailableError semantics, but intentionally retain distinct entry points so a route cannot preload the wrong authority through an untyped generic string.

The request-scoped edge counterparts of the refresh*FromPromoted bindings above: each seats a runner-published authority artifact into its OWN module cache for one reader request, binding a different type (RegistryRuntimeReadModel vs FederalDirectoryReadModel), domain validator, and isolated cache, and setting that module's read-state to BOOTSTRAP. A generic would take an untyped value into a caller-named cache — exactly the wrong-authority-through-a-string hazard the refresh group is kept separate to prevent — while duplicating no validation or cache policy.

Each synchronous accessor guards a different module-local cache and names the exact preload required. Their matching fail-closed shape is intentional; a shared accessor would need mutable cache parameters and could weaken the source-isolation boundary this cutover tests.

This is a structural coincidence across unrelated work: Admin concurrently reads three durable repositories, while the test helper constructs candidate, event, and promotion fixture arrays. They share no semantics or callable production helper, and coupling the test fixture to Admin would be the wrong dependency direction.

These are source-specific adapters binding different contracts, test fixtures, validators, and isolated read states to the already shared promoted-data reader. Keeping the shells separate preserves failure isolation between executive actions and meeting outcomes; the canonical store and bootstrap policy are not duplicated.
A third and fourth CSV parser, in lib this time. Travels with the scripts/ pair above.

React context accessors: useContext, throw if absent, return. Three lines each, identical by construction across every codebase that uses contexts. Consolidating would produce a generic that is longer than the thing it replaces.
Two readers of the Next build trace manifests. The build-budget guard and the trace census must be looking at the same population, and today each computes it.
Two database-verification scripts each print their own verdict. A shared reporter keeps the four-verdict discipline (green, red, pending, could-not-tell) identical between them.

These are isolated Playwright proof harnesses with different frozen denominators: the historical exhaustive reader census and the bounded final-delta visual sample. Sharing the navigation helper would make the delta proof import the exhaustive harness and expand LM-F1 proof rather than inheriting it; both harnesses assert the product identity and payload selectors independently.

The collision exists only once identifiers are erased: both return seven fields read off their argument. synthesisFields renames an Ask evidence pack into the model-facing synthesis vocabulary; promotedPointerIdentity narrows a civic-data pointer to its identity columns so Reader-delivery evidence never carries the promoted payload. They share no field, caller, or policy, and a common helper would couple the Ask prompt contract to the civic-data store boundary.

consolidatedOn2026-08-25.what: the gate runner, duplicated between the two scripts that bookend a session
consolidatedOn2026-08-25.how: Moved to scripts/try-run.mjs. Each caller keeps a one-line BINDING that supplies cwd and nothing else, which is not an implementation.
consolidatedOn2026-08-25.why: It was consolidated because the duplicate had already cost something: Node defaults execFileSync maxBuffer to 1 MB, output past it THROWS, and both copies turned that into null. docs/state.md crossed a megabyte, so every git show of it in the handoff mirror guard threw, every revision was skipped, and the guard reported that a byte-identical mirror copy matched no version in its history — failing the handoff, which under RULING 75 is a gate. Fixing one copy would have left the other carrying the same silent wrong answer.
